title: Tenet Diplos
extract:
The Tenet Diplos are unique Tenet akimbo pistols with fully automatic fire, an aimed fire mode that locks-on to enemies with burst-fire seeking projectiles, and is able to reload while holstered.

Characteristics
This weapon primarily deals  Impact damage.
Aiming activates lock-on mode, targeting up to 8 enemies within 60 meters on the reticle to burst-fire 2 shots of seeking projectiles per target.
Lock-on homing targets the enemy's body, making it difficult to achieve headshots unless aiming upward.
Lock-on projectiles must travel 5 meters before seeking.
Lock-on burst-fire consumes 4 ammo (2 per pistol) per target.
Lock-on has a ~0.5 second delay after the burst ends before being able to lock-on again (affected by fire rate).
Reloads 10% of its magazine per second while holstered.
Innate  polarity.
Adversary Weapon:
Comes with an additional bonus  Impact,  Heat,  Cold,  Electricity,  Toxin,  Magnetic, or  Radiation damage, based on the Sister's progenitor Warframe, which increases the listed base damage of the weapon by 25%-60%.
Valence Fusion can optionally change the resulting output damage type, and can upgrade the bonus increase (up to 60%).
Polarizing the weapon increases its max rank by 2, capping at rank 40 after 5 polarizations, granting the weapon additional mod capacity.
 Elemental Vice can be applied to the weapon after it has reached rank 40, allowing the bonus damage type to be swapped freely.
Listed Mastery Rank requirement is not enforced - the weapon may theoretically be obtained at any mastery rank by acquiring and vanquishing a Sister that has this weapon equipped.
Advantages over other Secondary   weapons (excluding modular weapons):

Pinpoint accuracy.
Innate 1 meter punch through.
Reloads 8 rounds per second while holstered.

Acquisition

Tenet Diplos is obtained by vanquishing a Sister who generated with one equipped. After the Sister is vanquished it will be in the player's Foundry ready to claim.
While the weapon itself is not tradeable, a converted Sister generated with the weapon can be traded to another player. The trade is performed inside a Clan Dojo's Crimson Branch room, and the recipient must not have any active Lich or Sister. Once traded, the recipient must fight and vanquish the Sister to claim their weapon.

Notes
Aiming toggles lock-on mode.
Up to a maximum of 8 targets can be locked-on by aiming at enemies within 60 meters, indicated by the circular reticle.
Locked-on targets are marked by a white diamond that flashes bright at successful home-in.
If the target moves ? meters away or dies while being aimed at, their lock-ons are removed.
Full-auto fire can still be used by firing from hip-fire and then zooming in or not aiming over an enemy to not trigger the lock-on.
Lock-on mode is disabled against targets with invulnerability, such as enemies being corrupted by a Void Fissure, as well as those taking cover inside a Nullifier bubble. It is, however, enabled for enemies protected by Arbitration Shield Drones.
Lock-on does not work with  Cyte-09's  Seek, targets cannot be acquired through walls and homing shots will not pierce walls.
While holstered, the attaché case's components will rumble and make an audible sound for each ammo reloaded.
Passive reload stacks with  Eject Magazine and the Synth Mod Set ( Synth Deconstruct,  Synth Fiber,  Synth Reflex and  Synth Charge).
Similar to the  Velox, these weapons are functionally silent despite having an "Alarming" noise level; they can be fired near enemies without alerting them unless a bullet hits a surface very close to them. However, they will still break  Ivara's  Prowl unless the  Suppress mod is equipped.

Adversary Notes
For weapons obtained from vanquishing the Kuva Lich or Sister:
The player does not have to meet the Mastery Rank displayed to obtain this weapon. It can simply be claimed from the foundry after the Lich/Sister carrying it has been vanquished.
The weapon will have a prefix of the name of the Lich/Sister it was acquired from (e.g. a Kuva Kohm might be called "Odizrigg Agekk Kuva Kohm").
Refraining from Mercy killing an Adversary candidate and letting them die will remove their weapon from the pool of potential Adversary weapons until each has been refused, but only if the mission is completed. Weapons rejected from aborted missions will remain in the current cycle.
It is also possible for the weapon to be removed from the cycle even without waiting for the Adversary candidate to die before extracting from the mission.
For weapons obtained from Ergo Glast's and Eleanor's shop:
The player must meet the Mastery Rank displayed to obtain this weapon, as it is claimed from an NPC shop rather than the foundry.
The weapon's max rank caps at 40 after 5 polarizations (max rank increases by 2 per Forma added).
Additional polarizations can be added when the weapon reaches its new max rank at that polarization level.
Each additional rank also gives 100 Mastery Rank experience, giving 4,000 points in total at level 40.
Mod capacity scales with the additional ranks, and can reach a total of 80 at rank 40 with an Orokin Catalyst installed.
Without an Orokin Catalyst, the max is 40. Combined with the five polarized mod slots required to reach that point, an Orokin Catalyst might not be required for some beginner-friendly builds as they typically use less mod capacity.
After polarizing a weapon, any additional mod capacity above 30 (60 with an Orokin Catalyst) will not take effect until the weapon's rank reaches 31 and above.
Legendary Mastery Rank increases the minimum mod capacity for such weapons, without the weapon needing to be rank 31 and above. For example, Legendary 1 increases the minimum capacity to 31 (62 with an Orokin Catalyst).
Comes with an additional damage stat.
For Lich/Sister-obtained weapons this is dependent on the Warframe that summoned the Lich/Sister.
For Ergo Glast's and Eleanor's shops a random bonus stat will be offered for each weapon and changed every 4 days (96 hours).
This damage stat randomly ranges between 25%-60%. It can be upgraded up to its maximum value with Valence Fusion using another copy of the weapon.
The element of this bonus can be changed at will among the available Valence elements once an Elemental Vice is applied.
This bonus stat is considered a base damage type and will be applied after all elemental mods for the purposes of elemental combinations. It uses the weapon's falloff range but always scales linearly from 100% to 0%, regardless of what the weapon's falloff damage scaling is.

*Note that the Primed or Umbra version of a Warframe share the same element

Known Bugs
 Galvanized Shot is multiplicative to base damage sources on direct hits from lock-on mode.

Tips
The Diplos has noticeable recoil, so it is recommended to fire the guns at short bursts or mitigate the recoil with  Steady Hands.
If not using lock-on mode, hip-firing and then ADS will grant the bonuses of aiming without enabling the lock-on mechanic.
When using lock-on mode, wait until the lock-on indicator flashes before pulling the trigger to ensure that the gun will not go full auto mode. This is particularly useful when in the middle of an encounter with too much visual noise, such as explosions from an allied player's weapons or being struck by a  Magnetic proc.
The Diplos cannot lock in on Arbitration Shield Drones, making the guns ineffective at disposing them. Additionally, the lock-on mode is enabled against enemies protected by the drone, wasting shots on invulnerable targets.
You can start hip firing then ADS to keep the Diplos full-auto to make use of mods like Galvanized Crosshairs easier.

Trivia
While holstered and while reloading, the weapon folds up into an attaché case.
The weapon's name means "twofold", referring to how the weapon folds when (un)sheathed.

Bugs
Aiming down sights away from an enemy and using an autoclicker or mousewheel to fire the weapon causes it to fire as fast as the inputs register. This has no practical application as moving the reticle over an enemy immediately causes the lock-on function to activate.
The Diplos used to be able to lock in on Arbitration Shield Drones, making the guns effective at disposing them. Additionally, the lock-on mode was disabled against enemies protected by the drone, preventing the player from wasting shots on invulnerable targets. This behavior has now been reversed. As it is an undocumented change, it is likely a bug.
